question.prompt: When a positive integer \(x\) is divided by a positive integer \(y,\) the quotient is \(u\) and the remainder is \(v,\) where \(u\) and \(v\) are integers. What is the remainder when \(x+2uy\) is divided by \(y?\)

solutions.explanation:
The given division means
\[
x=uy+v,\qquad 0\le v<y.
\]
Substitute this into the new dividend:
\[
x+2uy=uy+v+2uy=(3u)y+v.
\]
The added amount supplies whole multiples of \(y\). Since \(3u\) is an integer and \(v\) still satisfies \(0\le v<y\), the new quotient is \(3u\) and the remainder is \(\boxed{v}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Use the quotient and remainder
